summary: Both browser screenshots taken at 12:43 on the quartermaster branch confirm the build is red. In Screenshot 1 (clip: 0T-Pose -> meshyCharacter:FPS-REST-ARMS-CAL--120) the Meshy actor's right arm is raised but no saber is visible in the hand or anywhere in the scene. In Screenshot 2 (clip: OneHandReady -> meshyCharacter) the actor's pose differs materially from the previously accepted OneHandReady reference — the sword arm is not extended into a recognisable ready guard — and again no saber mesh is present. The weapon prop has disappeared across both clips and the OneHandReady pose has regressed. PR #2 must not be merged.

visual_findings.title: Saber mesh absent in both clips
visual_findings.evidence: Screenshot 1 (0T-Pose clip): right hand raised, no saber geometry visible anywhere in the viewport. Screenshot 2 (OneHandReady clip): actor visible, no saber geometry visible anywhere in the viewport.
visual_findings.review_comment: The saber prop is not rendering for the Meshy Character actor under either tested clip. This is a complete weapon-visibility regression. The prop attachment, socket binding, or visibility flag introduced or modified by this PR has broken saber display. Do not merge until the saber is confirmed visible in-viewport for every clip that previously showed it.

visual_findings.title: OneHandReady pose regressed from accepted reference
visual_findings.evidence: Screenshot 2 (OneHandReady -> meshyCharacter): the actor's sword arm is not in the previously accepted extended one-hand-ready guard position. The pose reads as a relaxed or neutral stance, not a combat-ready pose.
visual_findings.review_comment: The OneHandReady clip pose no longer matches the accepted visual reference. Whether this is caused by a bone transform change, a clip data overwrite, or a rig-binding side-effect of this PR is inconclusive from screenshots alone, but the regression is visually confirmed. The pose must be restored to the accepted reference before re-review.

visual_findings.title: 0T-Pose clip arm position inconsistent with expected calibration rest
visual_findings.evidence: Screenshot 1 (0T-Pose -> meshyCharacter:FPS-REST-ARMS-CAL--120): the right arm/hand is raised rather than in a neutral T or rest position expected for a calibration clip.
visual_findings.review_comment: The calibration rest clip is showing an unexpected raised-arm pose. This may indicate the clip data was overwritten or the bone offsets were altered as a side-effect of this PR. Inconclusive without diff of clip asset, but warrants explicit verification against the pre-PR baseline.

process_findings.title: PR merged/deployed without passing visual gate
process_findings.evidence: Source packet states prior static/code review found PR #2 narrow but not visually accepted. Screenshots taken post-deployment still show red build.
process_findings.review_comment: The branch was deployed to the local preview server before visual acceptance criteria were met. The process gate requiring a passing visual screenshot review before deployment was bypassed. No PR should advance to preview deployment without an explicit visual sign-off on all affected clips.

process_findings.title: Contract/unit-test passage treated as proxy for visual correctness
process_findings.evidence: Source packet explicitly notes: 'Do not treat source-string tests, socket markers, or local hilt traces as proof of visual success.' The PR was advanced after contract failures were addressed, implying test-green was used as a merge signal.
process_findings.review_comment: Passing automated tests is a necessary but not sufficient condition for this class of visual/animation work. The review process must require a human visual confirmation screenshot for every clip touched by the PR before the build is considered green. Test passage alone must not gate advancement.

process_findings.title: No before/after visual comparison attached to PR
process_findings.evidence: No reference screenshots showing the accepted pre-PR state of the OneHandReady pose or saber visibility were attached to PR #2 per the source packet.
process_findings.review_comment: PRs that touch weapon attachment, pose clips, or rig bindings must include side-by-side before/after viewport screenshots for every affected clip as part of the PR description. Without a baseline reference, reviewers cannot confirm regression at review time and must rely on memory.

process_findings.title: Scope of clip regression not bounded — other clips not verified
process_findings.evidence: Only two of the four listed clips (0T-Pose and OneHandReady) were screenshotted. Clips 'Armature|running|baselayer' and 'Armature|walking_man|baselayer' were not visually verified.
process_findings.review_comment: When a PR touches weapon attachment or rig binding, all clips for the affected actor must be visually verified, not just the two most obvious ones. The remaining two clips must be screenshotted and reviewed before any re-submission is considered.

what_not_to_do_next: Do not merge PR #2 in its current state.
Do not start another edit cycle on the quartermaster branch without first reverting to the last known-good visual baseline and confirming the saber is visible.
Do not use passing unit tests, socket-marker logs, or hilt-trace output as evidence that the visual build is green.
Do not deploy to the preview server again until a visual gate screenshot has been reviewed and explicitly signed off.
Do not submit a revised PR without attaching before/after viewport screenshots for every clip on the Meshy Character actor.
Do not treat the OneHandReady pose as acceptable in its current regressed state — do not attempt to redefine the acceptance criteria to match the regressed pose.
minimum_next_review_gate: A new review may only be opened after: (1) the saber mesh is confirmed visible in-viewport for all Meshy Character clips that previously displayed it, captured in a timestamped screenshot; (2) the OneHandReady pose is confirmed to match the previously accepted reference, captured in a side-by-side comparison screenshot; (3) all four listed clips are screenshotted and attached to the PR; and (4) a reviewer who did not author the fix has signed off on all three screenshot sets before any deployment to the preview server.
